nodes.summary: Required protocol operations fail to make progress.
nodes.definition: An otherwise eligible operation cannot complete under the intended lifecycle.

nodes.summary: Protocol accounting diverges from economic state.
nodes.definition: Recorded claims, obligations, or payments disagree with their specified economic meaning.

nodes.summary: Liquidation fails its intended economic function.
nodes.definition: Unhealthy positions require a viable settlement mechanism.

nodes.summary: Eligible withdrawals cannot complete.
nodes.definition: Withdrawal controls prevent intended exits.

nodes.summary: Eligible operations retain a completion path.
nodes.definition: Lifecycle transitions preserve intended progress.

nodes.summary: Claims reflect recoverable economic value.
nodes.definition: Recognized claims reconcile with assets and realized losses.

nodes.summary: Liquidation compensation uses consistent units.
nodes.definition: Compensation follows the documented reward model.

nodes.summary: Liquidation rewards mix debt and collateral denominations.
nodes.definition: A reward formula combines values measured in different token units. Decimal scaling then changes compensation and can remove the intended liquidation incentive. Normalize values into the payout denomination before applying reward arithmetic.
applicability: Debt and collateral use different denominations.
exclusions: Low market profitability alone does not establish a formula defect.

nodes.summary: Collateral delisting disables existing withdrawals.
nodes.definition: A listing check intended for admission also gates exit. Removing support then prevents withdrawal of previously accepted collateral. Separate admission policy from safe unwind eligibility.
applicability: Collateral can be delisted after deposit.
exclusions: Explicit temporary freezes with a documented exit process require separate assessment.

nodes.summary: Residual debt has no loss-recognition path.
nodes.definition: After collateral exhaustion, residual debt remains booked without a settlement or write-off path. Accounting continues to treat unrecoverable obligations as value. Define explicit loss recognition for terminal debt states.
applicability: Liquidation can exhaust collateral before debt.
exclusions: Bad debt itself is not proof that its accounting is incorrect.

nodes.summary: Withdrawal counters and reset state have different scopes.
nodes.definition: Per-user usage counters rely on a shared period-reset marker. Period rollover may leave individual counters stale. Track period membership consistently with the scope of each quota.
applicability: Withdrawals use periodically renewed user quotas.
exclusions: An intentionally shared global quota is a different policy.

nodes.summary: Deposit credit exceeds the assets actually received.
nodes.definition: Accounting credits a requested transfer amount although token mechanics reduce net receipts. Claims and downstream accounting become inconsistent with backing. Reconcile credited value with actual supported-token receipt semantics.
applicability: Supported assets may charge transfer fees.
exclusions: A reliably enforced exclusion of such assets removes this prerequisite.

nodes.summary: Size liquidation compensation used inconsistent units.
nodes.definition: Size H-04 reports denomination-mismatched rewards. The sponsor confirmed the finding and reported a fix in PR 118.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments.

nodes.summary: INIT delisting could block existing collateral withdrawals.
nodes.definition: INIT M-09 was acknowledged. The report narrows the remaining impact to withdrawals under the sponsor’s stated delisting sequence.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments.

nodes.summary: INIT lacked residual debt settlement after collateral exhaustion.
nodes.definition: INIT M-10 reports unhandled remaining debt affecting pool accounting. The sponsor confirmed it.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments.

nodes.summary: prePO user withdrawal counters could remain stale.
nodes.definition: prePO H-01 reports inconsistent reset scope; the sponsor confirmed the finding.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments.

nodes.summary: prePO deposit credit could exceed net token receipts.
nodes.definition: prePO M-02 concerns transfer-fee assets. The sponsor confirmed it; the judge assigned Medium severity.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments.

nodes.summary: Partial liquidation leaves a subeconomic residual position.
nodes.definition: A permitted partial liquidation can leave debt or collateral too small for a profitable follow-up liquidation. Test whether closeout rules, reward design, and lender claims retain a viable cleanup path; a permissive dust override alone does not require cleanup.
applicability: Liquidation can partially settle a borrower position.
Follow-up settlement has per-position transaction costs.
exclusions: Dust does not automatically become bad debt when borrower debt does not passively accrue.
A subsidized or batched cleanup path can change the economic conclusion.

nodes.summary: Offer fills create many uneconomic borrower debts.
nodes.definition: An offer accepts arbitrarily small exposure-creating fills across borrower positions, while the minimum-size rule applies only during liquidation. One lender claim can then depend on many separate, unprofitable settlements. Enforce exposure sizing at admission or provide an economically viable aggregate recovery path.
applicability: A maker offer can be filled in small amounts by multiple borrowers.
Recovery settles one borrower per transaction.
exclusions: A liquidation-time dust rule does not by itself constrain debt creation.
Small positions alone do not prove recovery is uneconomic on every host chain.

nodes.summary: Liquidation targets collateral that can move before execution.
nodes.definition: A liquidator selects a collateral index from an earlier view of a borrower position. If collateral can be rotated after maturity, the named index can become empty before execution and the transaction reverts. Check whether execution-time selection or route design avoids stale targets.
applicability: A borrower can change collateral composition after maturity.
Liquidation specifies a particular collateral index.
exclusions: A smart-contract liquidator that reads the current position atomically can neutralize this stale-index path.
A reverting fixed-index attempt is not proof that all liquidation routes are blocked.

nodes.summary: Fresh credit inherits a terminal historical loss.
nodes.definition: An obligation remains open to new credit after its loss accumulator reaches a terminal state. Applying that accumulator to newly entered credit can extinguish principal for a loss that predates entry. Guard new exposure at terminal states or reset accounting for a valid new epoch.
applicability: Loss accumulation can saturate while an obligation remains fillable.
exclusions: A loss applying only to incumbents is expected and distinct from slashing new credit.

nodes.summary: New vault deposits fund exits during unresolved losses.
nodes.definition: An allocator deposits into a vault without checking pending losses in underlying positions. Fresh assets may supply exit liquidity for existing holders while the allocator retains claims it later cannot redeem fully. Check loss recognition and backing before allocating capital.
applicability: A vault can have unrealized bad debt in underlying positions.
New deposits can be used to satisfy existing withdrawals.
exclusions: A healthy vault or a reliable loss-aware entry policy removes this prerequisite.
The finding concerns an allocator depositing into a third-party vault, not every vault deposit.

nodes.summary: Emergency pause also disables debt repayment.
nodes.definition: A pause guard intended to halt risky adapter activity also gates repayment. An existing borrower or module then cannot reduce exposure or complete an unwind while the pause remains active. Separate safe debt settlement from the prohibited paused actions.
applicability: Repayment routes through a pausable adapter.
Existing positions may need to unwind during a pause.
exclusions: A deliberate debt-settlement freeze with an alternative safe repayment path requires separate assessment.

nodes.summary: Morpho Midnight liquidation could leave dust debt or collateral.
nodes.definition: Cantina Solo 3.1.1 reported residual dust after partial liquidation. Morpho added documentation in PR 991 and chose not to change the mechanism; StErMi acknowledged. The report identifies possible future price, withdrawal, and oracle-liveness effects, not automatic bad debt.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments.

nodes.summary: Morpho Midnight allowed debt fragmentation below its dust threshold.
nodes.definition: Cantina Competition 3.1.5 reported small offer fills across borrower positions, while the recovery threshold applied only during liquidation. Morpho acknowledged the mechanism and said it was insufficiently documented.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments or universal liquidation costs.

nodes.summary: Morpho Midnight post-maturity collateral rotation could invalidate fixed-index liquidation.
nodes.definition: Cantina Competition 3.1.8 reported a stale selected collateral index. Morpho agreed that such a transaction can revert but assessed repeated delay as unlikely and noted atomic position reads by smart-contract liquidators as mitigation.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot only.
exclusions: No claim that all liquidation paths fail or that lender loss is inevitable.

nodes.summary: Morpho Midnight new lender credit could be slashed by a prior terminal loss.
nodes.definition: Blackthorn M-1 reported fresh entry into an obligation with saturated loss index. The report marks the issue resolved and cites Morpho PR 743 as the fix.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot only.
exclusions: No independent verification of the reported fix or claim about current deployments.

nodes.summary: Bitcorn allocator could deposit into a Morpho vault with unresolved bad debt.
nodes.definition: Cantina Managed 3.1.1 found the module borrowed assets for a MetaMorpho deposit without checking underlying losses. The report says Bitcorn fixed this in PR 111 and Cantina verified the fix.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments beyond the report disposition.

nodes.summary: Bitcorn pause blocked its module repayment path.
nodes.definition: Cantina Managed 3.2.1 reported that the adapter pause guard also reached repayment, preventing the module from unwinding an open borrow. The report says Bitcorn fixed this in commit a29178f and Cantina verified the fix.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments beyond the report disposition.

nodes.summary: Expired rate schedule erases unaccrued interest.
nodes.definition: An interest controller returns zero after its deadline even when the next accrual spans time before that deadline. Earned interest from the earlier interval is omitted from recognized assets and share redemptions. Accrue each elapsed interval under the rate that applied to it.
applicability: Interest accrues lazily when a user or administrator interacts.
A scheduled rate ends before the next accrual.
exclusions: A checkpoint at the deadline or carry-forward of earned interest removes this path.

nodes.summary: Loss realization compares values from different accrual epochs.
nodes.definition: Adapter allocation accounting updates on allocation changes while vault total assets also accrue interest between those changes. Comparing stale allocation against current redeemable value can revert or understate realized loss, leaving vault assets overstated. Reconcile valuation epochs before recognizing a loss.
applicability: Vault interest accrues without synchronizing adapter allocations.
Loss recognition uses adapter allocation as its baseline.
exclusions: An adapter baseline updated with the same accrual events removes this mismatch.

nodes.summary: Cash inflow masks an adapter loss before it is realized again.
nodes.definition: A vault interest controller estimates profit from the net change in cash and adapter value. When excess cash masks an adapter loss, the loss first suppresses profit that would otherwise be credited; a separate loss-realization call then deducts the same loss. Reconcile cash and adapter changes into one economic delta before updating share value.
applicability: Cash balance can exceed recorded idle assets through donations or deallocation penalties.
Profit estimation and loss realization use separate baselines.
exclusions: If the cash and adapter baselines are synchronized before either update, this double-counting path is absent.

nodes.summary: Morpho Vault V2 manual interest controller could omit pre-deadline accrual.
nodes.definition: Cantina Vault V2 Competition 3.1.1 reported that a lazy accrual after the manual controller deadline could omit interest earned before it. The final report assigns Medium severity and contains no sponsor disposition for this finding.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot at commit 5938a924 only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments or remediation.

nodes.summary: Morpho Vault V2 adapter allocation lagged accrued vault assets during loss realization.
nodes.definition: Cantina Vault V2 Competition 3.1.2 reported that allocation state lagged interest already included in total assets, making loss realization revert or underreport losses. The final report assigns Medium severity and contains no sponsor disposition for this finding.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot at commit 5938a924 only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments or remediation.

nodes.summary: Morpho Vault V2 controller could count a masked adapter loss twice.
nodes.definition: Cantina Vault V2 Competition 3.1.3 reported that excess vault cash could mask an adapter loss during interest estimation, before realizeLoss deducted it again. The final report assigns Medium severity and contains no sponsor disposition for this finding.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot at commit 5938a924 only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments or remediation.

nodes.summary: Interest-rate state diverges from the intended model.
nodes.definition: State transitions in an interest-rate model can alter borrowing and lending economics without the utilization or policy change the model expects.
applicability: Protocol uses a stateful interest-rate model.

nodes.summary: Public rate-model update trusts caller-supplied market state.
nodes.definition: A stateful rate-model update is callable outside its owning lending market and accepts debt, collateral, or time inputs from that caller. An attacker can move the model state without an authorized market transition. Bind state updates to the canonical market caller and its observed inputs.
applicability: Interest-rate updates are stateful and exposed through a public entrypoint.
exclusions: A read-only quotation function cannot directly mutate the model state.
An enforced market-only caller check removes this path.

nodes.summary: Pending configuration changes live rate state early.
nodes.definition: Scheduling a timelocked rate-model configuration also mutates a live model parameter before the activation time. Rates change under an unactivated policy, and cancellation may leave the mutated state behind. Stage dependent state with the pending configuration and apply both at activation.
applicability: Rate configuration has delayed activation or cancellation.
Scheduling mutates live model state.
exclusions: An intentionally immediate parameter change is a different policy.

nodes.summary: Silo dynamic kink state update lacked a market-only caller check.
nodes.definition: Cantina reported that getCompoundInterestRateAndUpdate accepted calls and rate inputs from parties other than the Silo, allowing the kink state to change outside its intended market update. The review assigns High severity and marks the finding fixed.
applicability: Historical reviewed version only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments or independent verification of the fix.

nodes.summary: Silo pending rate configuration reset the live kink early.
nodes.definition: Cantina reported that scheduling a delayed configuration immediately reset the live k parameter to the new minimum, so even cancellation could leave interest rates changed. The review assigns Medium severity and marks the finding fixed.
applicability: Historical reviewed version only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments or independent verification of the fix.

nodes.summary: Validator registry state diverges from the active consensus set.
nodes.definition: Validator identity, enumeration, or lifecycle state no longer represents the participants intended to secure consensus.
applicability: Protocol maintains an onchain validator registry.

nodes.summary: Each validator identity has a unique consensus key.
nodes.definition: The registry prevents two validator records from representing the same consensus signing identity.
applicability: Consensus attributes participation by registered public key.

nodes.summary: Arbitrary recipient actions refresh a target's restriction.
nodes.definition: A permissionless operation lets its caller choose a recipient and refreshes that recipient's action lock as a side effect. Repeated dust operations can keep a user or protocol contract unable to transfer and can block dependent workflows. Require recipient consent or avoid extending restrictions from unsolicited state changes.
applicability: A caller can mint or credit a minimal amount to an arbitrary address.
Receipt extends a transfer or action restriction for that address.
exclusions: A restriction applied only to the consenting caller removes this griefing path.

nodes.summary: A same-epoch state transition earns rewards in both states.
nodes.definition: A position receives an epoch's reward in its source state, then moves to another state whose accounting treats it as present for that same epoch. The position captures the distribution twice and dilutes other participants. Give each position one reward-bearing state at every epoch boundary.
applicability: Rewards are accounted separately across lifecycle modules.
A position can transition after one module accrues but before the epoch ends.
exclusions: A transition checkpoint that excludes the destination from the current epoch removes this path.

nodes.summary: Sequential allocation mutates the shared denominator.
nodes.definition: A loop allocates one economic total across buckets but reduces the denominator after each bucket. Later allocations use a larger effective fraction, so their sum can exceed the intended loss or payment and corrupt aggregate state. Compute all proportional shares from one immutable baseline.
applicability: One amount is distributed proportionally across multiple buckets.
exclusions: A true remainder-allocation algorithm that reduces both numerator and denominator consistently is distinct.

nodes.summary: Cancellation subtracts a scheduled delta before application.
nodes.definition: A lifecycle cancellation removes a position's scheduled slope or weight from aggregate state before the corresponding scheduled addition has been processed. Persisting that premature subtraction corrupts later accounting and can cause underflow. Cancel pending deltas in their schedule or first advance aggregate state through the effective boundary.
applicability: Aggregate state advances lazily across scheduled epoch deltas.
A position can cancel at the first effective epoch.
exclusions: Cancellation after the scheduled addition is incorporated uses a different state transition.

nodes.summary: Partial settlement rounds liability reduction down.
nodes.definition: A partial fill consumes an exact amount of assets but rounds down the receipt or claim amount removed. The remaining claim is overstated, and repeated fills can accumulate unbacked value. Choose rounding direction to ensure consumed assets reduce liability by at least their corresponding amount.
applicability: Claims are partially fulfilled through a fixed-point conversion ratio.
exclusions: Rounding dust explicitly charged to the claimant under a bounded policy is distinct.

nodes.summary: A privileged operator bypasses delegated beneficiary routing.
nodes.definition: A payout or unstake path defaults its recipient to the operator and resolves the delegated beneficiary only for other callers. The operator can therefore redirect principal or rewards supplied by the beneficiary. Derive the economic recipient from stake ownership independently of caller authorization.
applicability: One party operates a position funded by another party.
Both parties may call claim or unstake functions.
exclusions: A documented arrangement that assigns the operator the funds is a different beneficiary policy.

nodes.summary: Live-count bounds skip sparse monotonic identifiers.
nodes.definition: Enumeration scans identifiers from one through the current live item count even though burns create gaps without reusing later identifiers. Existing records above the reduced count disappear from registry-derived operations. Enumerate live IDs directly or bound scans by the highest allocated identifier.
applicability: Identifiers increase monotonically and records can be burned.
Registry scans use live supply as the maximum identifier.
exclusions: Dense identifiers that are reassigned on deletion do not have this gap.

nodes.summary: A terminal penalty path refunds an uncleared balance.
nodes.definition: A penalty branch ejects and unstakes a participant when the penalty reaches their full balance, but does not clear that balance before the generic unstake routine pays it out. The terminal branch therefore refunds value intended to be slashed. Apply the penalty to canonical balance state before invoking shared exit logic.
applicability: A full penalty enters a separate ejection or burn path.
That path reuses a routine that returns the recorded balance.
exclusions: An explicitly documented lenient force-exit policy is distinct from penalty enforcement.

nodes.summary: Epoch settlement mixes parameters from different versions.
nodes.definition: A configuration update changes one parameter read at settlement immediately, while a related parameter was snapshotted from the old version at epoch start. The epoch is settled under neither complete policy and can overpay or underpay. Snapshot all coupled parameters under one version at the same boundary.
applicability: Epoch economics depend on multiple coupled configuration fields.
Fields are read at different points in the epoch lifecycle.
exclusions: Independent parameters intentionally activated at different times require separate policy analysis.

nodes.summary: Validator registration accepts a reused consensus key.
nodes.definition: The registry creates multiple validator identities for the same consensus public key. Committee membership can then overstate independent participation, while duplicate signatures or discovery records conflict. Reserve each consensus key to one live validator identity at registration.
applicability: Onchain registration accepts a consensus public key.
Committee security assumes distinct signing identities.
exclusions: Key rotation that atomically retires the old association is not duplicate live registration.

nodes.summary: InfiniFi arbitrary minting could repeatedly restrict a target.
nodes.definition: Cantina reported that minting a minimal amount to an arbitrary address refreshed its action restriction, allowing repeated denial of user and protocol-contract transfers. The review assigns High severity, marks the finding fixed, and records Cantina's fix as OK.
applicability: Historical reviewed version only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments beyond the report disposition.

nodes.summary: InfiniFi same-epoch unwinding could claim one reward distribution twice.
nodes.definition: Cantina reported that a position rewarded in LockingController could enter UnwindingModule later in the same epoch and be counted again for that epoch. The review assigns High severity, marks the finding fixed, and records Cantina's fix as OK.
applicability: Historical reviewed version only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments beyond the report disposition.

nodes.summary: InfiniFi loss allocation used a progressively smaller denominator.
nodes.definition: Cantina reported that LockingController decremented its local global-receipt total while using it as each epoch bucket's allocation denominator, over-allocating losses and corrupting totals. The review assigns High severity, marks the finding fixed, and records Cantina's fix as OK.
applicability: Historical reviewed version only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments beyond the report disposition.

nodes.summary: InfiniFi first-epoch unwinding cancellation could corrupt reward slopes.
nodes.definition: Cantina reported that cancelUnwinding could subtract a reward-weight decrease in its first effective epoch before the scheduled decrease had been processed, corrupting rewards and potentially causing underflow denial of service. The review assigns High severity, marks the finding fixed, and records Cantina's fix as OK.
applicability: Historical reviewed version only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments beyond the report disposition.

nodes.summary: InfiniFi partial redemption rounded the receipt burn down.
nodes.definition: Cantina reported that partial funding consumed available assets while rounding down the corresponding receipt-token burn, overstating the remaining redemption request. The review assigns Medium severity, marks the finding fixed, and records Cantina's fix as OK.
applicability: Historical reviewed version only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments beyond the report disposition.

nodes.summary: Telcoin validators could redirect delegated stake and rewards to themselves.
nodes.definition: Cantina reported that claim and unstake defaulted the recipient to the validator and checked delegation only for non-validator callers, bypassing the stake originator. The review assigns High severity and marks the finding fixed.
applicability: Historical reviewed version only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments or independent reproduction.

nodes.summary: Telcoin token ID gaps could hide active validators from enumeration.
nodes.definition: Cantina reported that validator scans stopped at live totalSupply even though burns left gaps below later token IDs, omitting active validators from lifecycle and committee operations. The review assigns High severity and marks the finding fixed.
applicability: Historical reviewed version only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments or independent reproduction.

nodes.summary: Telcoin terminal slashing could return the balance intended to be penalized.
nodes.definition: Cantina reported that the full-slash ejection path did not zero the validator balance before generic unstaking returned it. Telcoin stated that the behavior had been intentional but changed the policy; the review assigns High severity and marks the finding fixed.
applicability: Historical reviewed version only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments or independent reproduction.

nodes.summary: Telcoin current-epoch rewards could combine new issuance with old duration.
nodes.definition: Cantina reported that a StakeConfig update changed issuance immediately while epoch duration remained the value captured for the current epoch, producing a mixed reward policy. The review assigns Medium severity and marks the finding fixed.
applicability: Historical reviewed version only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments or independent reproduction.

nodes.summary: Telcoin allowed multiple validators to register one BLS key.
nodes.definition: Cantina reported that validator registration did not enforce BLS public-key uniqueness, allowing duplicate committee identities that could reduce effective committee size and fault tolerance. The review assigns Medium severity and marks the finding fixed.
applicability: Historical reviewed version only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments or independent reproduction.
